name: Grian

attributes.attribute: Irish goddess whose name means sun
found in the place-names Tuamgraney and Lough Graney
goddess described as the sister of Grian

sources: Condren, Mary. The Serpent and the Goddess: Women, Religion and Power in Ancient Ireland. San Francisco: Harper & Row, 1989, 35.
O’Rahilly, Thomas. Early Irish History and Mythology. Dublin: The Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies, 1946, 289.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Grian is an Irish goddess whose name holds the plain sense of sun. Although many readers seek a sun god among the Celts, stronger clues name the sun as a goddess in Ireland. Her name rings like the word green, so spots such as Pallas Green near the fairy mound of Knockainy may use it. She appears in the place-names Tuamgraney and Lough Graney. Some call her the sister of the goddess Áine, Queen of Lough Gur.

okr.objective: Write the Irish sun goddess Grian and her traces in place-names and kinship.
key_results: Grian bears the solar name that means sun.
She appears in the place-names Tuamgraney and Lough Graney.
Some name her the sister of Áine, Fairy Queen of Lough Gur.
